ReasonforDeviation_Q2: In terms of overall over and under expenditure as of the end of September 2024, three departments were the main contributors to under expenditure against their projections namely: the Departments of Economic Development, Environmental Affairs and Tourism underspent by R204.900 million, Transport by R272.963 million and the Education by R77.587 million.

In respect of the remedial measures, the infrastructure bottlenecks identified will continue to be progressively escalated through the recently established institutional structures for Infrastructure:
i.e. through the Departmental Provincial Steering Committees (PISCs) and thereafter for further
intervention and escalation to the Technical Provincial Infrastructure Coordination Council (TPICC) and Provincial Infrastructure Coordinating Council (PICC) for final resolution. As such the PICC institutional structures need to continue to undertake robust monitoring of project statuses
such that the progression of the projects through the various IDMS stages materialize and where required recovery plans are initiated, and the projects lists amended through the upcoming
ReasonforDeviation_Q3: Departments were advised through provincial structures such as PISC, TPICC, Sub CBC, CBC and EXCO to ensure that they monitor closely their existing projects and implement their procurement plans to ensure that the pipeline of project for the financial year is committed to begin realizing expenditure.
ReasonforDeviation_Q4: The infrastructure unit under achieved by 0.65 per cent compared to the target of 98 per cent for this indicator. The under achievement of 0.65 per cent was due to under expenditure of four departments, the Department of Transport by R191.772 million, Department of Health by R81.231 million, Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture (DSRAC) by R31.245 million and Social Development by R10.782 million.
CorrectiveAction_Q4:
Although the target of 98 per cent was not achieved by marginal 0.65 per cent, the infrastructure expenditure over the last three financial years reflects improvements from 90.72 per cent in 2021/22, 90.97 per cent in 2022/23 and 93.65 per cent in 2023/24. The preliminary outcome of 97.35 per cent in 2024/25 shows a significant improvement of 3.7 per cent compared to the audited outcome of 2023/24. 
In the 2025/26 FY  APP  the targets for this indicator was revised to 90 per cent.
In respect of the remedial measures, the infrastructure bottlenecks identified will continue to be progressively escalated through institutional structures for Infrastructure i.e. through the Departmental Provincial Steering Committees (PISCs) and thereafter for further intervention and escalation to the Technical Premiers Infrastructure Coordination Council (T-PICC) and Premiers Infrastructure Coordinating Council (PICC) for final resolution.

ReasonforDeviation_Summary:
